another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent

Great! To get started, I need to know about the children you're claiming for.

**First, let me ask: How old is your child (or the youngest child if you have more than one)?**

Please tell me their age, and I'll be able to guide you through the eligibility requirements. The age categories we consider are:
- **Under 16 years old**
- **16 to 19 years old**
- **20 years old or over**

Once I know the ages, we can work through the specific eligibility criteria together.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and wanted to check if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who is 6 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have Alex, who is 6 years old - that's helpful.

Since Alex is under 16, let me move through the assessment to check the eligibility criteria.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent

conversation.author: actor

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status, as this is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me: Do you normally live in the UK?**

If not, I'll need to ask some follow-up questions about your residency status. There are several pathways that can make you eligible even if you don't normally reside in the UK, including:
- Having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (if applicable)
- Being a Crown servant living abroad
- Other specific circumstances

For now, let me start with whether you normally live in the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK - I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, I need to explore which specific residency pathways might apply to you.

Let me ask you a few questions to determine if you qualify under any of the special circumstances:

**1. Are you a Crown servant (working for the UK government) living abroad, or living in one of the qualifying countries?**

**2. Alternatively, do you have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

These are the main pathways that could make you eligible for Child Benefit while living abroad. Let me know which, if any, of these apply to you, and I can guide you through the appropriate checks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or working for the UK government abroad. And no, I don't have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme either.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Based on your situation, it appears you don't meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me confirm this is correct:

You are:
- Currently living abroad
- Not a Crown servant or UK government employee
- Not covered by the EU Settlement Scheme

Unfortunately, this means you don't satisfy any of the pathways available for residency eligibility. Child Benefit requires that you either normally live in the UK or meet one of the specific special circumstances, which you've indicated don't apply to you.

Let me navigate to the outcome to confirm:

---

## **Assessment Result: INELIGIBLE**

I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

### **Reason:**
While Alex meets all the child-specific eligibility criteria (being under 16, not working, not receiving benefits in their own right, and not in a disqualifying apprenticeship), **you do not meet the residency requirements** for Child Benefit.

### **What's Required:**
To qualify for Child Benefit, you must normally live in the UK **OR** meet one of these special circumstances:
- Have **settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Have **pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme (with qualifying conditions such as working, studying, or having sufficient resources)
- Be a **Crown servant** living and working abroad for a UK government department
- Be living in certain qualifying countries as a Crown servant

### **Your Situation:**
You're currently living abroad and don't meet any of these special residency pathways.

### **Next Steps:**
If your circumstances change and you move back to the UK, or if you acquire one of the qualifying statuses mentioned above, you would become eligible for Child Benefit. You can reapply when your residency situation changes.

For more information, you can visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

If you have any questions or if your circumstances change in the future, feel free to get in touch!
